To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ER-mediated Ca2+ release can selectively enhance LTD induction at CA1 synapses, thereby acting as a braking mechanism for LTP.
the presence of IP3-sensitive endoplasmic Ca2+ stores in CA1 spines can locally tune Ca-based plasticity, and selectively enhance long-term depression (LTD) induction.

the presence of intracellular calcium stores can locally modulate plasticity at individual synapses, and that this mechanism can promote synaptic re-use by preventing runaway strengthening at potent synapses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential role of ER in the local regulation and stabilization of synaptic plasticity in CA1 spines.
the functional implications of the spatial distribution of ER within dendritic spines.
the role of intracellular Ca2+ stores in the local regulation and stabilization of synaptic plasticity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of IP3 receptors in the dendritic spine may provide a brake to the runaway strengthening of potentiated synapses.

ER in the spine can locally regulate the dynamics of plasticity in a graded and input-specific fashion, and that the resulting changes in plasticity dynamics can promote the re-use of synapse strengths.
the ER in spines may be involved in the regulation of synaptic strength, but further experimental studies are necessary.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ER is not just a passive reservoir for calcium, but rather a dynamic structure that actively regulates the plasticity of individual CA1 synapse.

the presence of IP3-sensitive ER in spines is a key factor in the regulation of synaptic plasticity, and may be a critical element in the maintenance of a healthy balance between strengthening and weakening at potentiated synapse.

ER-mediated metaplasticity may be a critical component of the hippocampal circuitry that allows it to function as a reliable memory system, while maintaining a degree of flexibility that is necessary for learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Ca2+ stores may be a local, activity-regulated mechanism for controlling the dynamics of synaptic plasticity, and may be a key factor in the regulation of memory consolidation. © 2018, Saha et al.

the presence of IP3-sensitive stores can modulate Ca2+ dynamics and plasticity in a manner that is dependent on the local spine Ca2+ concentration, the Ca2+ buffering capacity of the spine, and the Ca2+ concentration in the dendritic shaft.
ER-mediated regulation of Ca2+ dynamics may be a critical factor for the local regulation of Ca2+-based synaptic plasticity.
